children: The Federal Reserve's post-GFC forward guidance structures have caused significant damage and should be eliminated or radically overhauled, said Jim Bianco, president and founder of Bianco Research.
Forward guidance, he said, has caused more damage “than the problems it has solved."
He cited how forward guidance kept the central bank from hiking interest rates in 2021 and early 2022 when inflation was mistakenly labeled as "transitory."
According to Bianco, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh does not believe in forward guidance and would be better off canceling the post-meeting press conference altogether.

"He'd be better off canceling the presser, but the institutional prerogative tells them not to, so every press conference is a useless mess, as he has no forward guidance to offer, no one knows what to ask him if he's not giving forward guidance," he said.

While the chairman refrains from offering forward guidance, other FOMC members continue to guide markets through public speeches, according to the strategist. He noted that New York Fed President John Williams and Vice Chairman Philip Jefferson offered forward guidance to the Fed holding at the recent meeting, while Fed Governor Chris Waller had previously provided guidance leading into the September rate hike.
The Fed should ditch or radically shorten its self-imposed blackout period of not talking in public, according to Bianco.
He said blackout periods only made sense "when everybody was supposed to clear the way for the chairman to speak because he was the voice that spoke for the committee."
That's no longer the case, as the committee has seen “sobering discussions” and "family fights," with more dissenting votes against the majority than any year since 1982, according to the strategist.

"We've inverted Fed communication," Bianco said. "The least important voice now is the chairman because he's not offering forward guidance," while the other 18 FOMC members deliver the real forward guidance once the blackout period lifts.

title: FOMC’s forward guidance has caused more problems than it has solved, says Jim Bianco
